newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Pharm shares fall after placement.
newsitem.headline: China Pharm shares fall after placement.

text.p: Shares of Vitamin C maker China Pharmaceutical Enterprise & Investment Corp Ltd fell on profit-taking on Wednesday after the company announced a plan to place 168 million new shares, brokers said.
The shares, which resumed trading on Wednesday after a one-day suspension, were down HK$0.01 to HK$1.42 just before the midday break. Volume was 202 million shares.
Brokers said investors were taking profit after the recent rally and that the drop in the share price would help narrow the gap between the placement price and the trading price.
The shares gained 16.13 percent last week.

The company said it would issue 168 million new shares to its controlling shareholder Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Group Co Ltd at HK$1.2768 per share after the parent agreed to place out the same number of existing company shares at HK$1.33 each.
"The deal is seen positive for its longer term growth," said Sean Li, associate director from Amsteel Securities. "A dilution fear is likely to be offset by its future earnings outlook."
The company said net proceeds from the new issue would be used to fund a possible acquisition of businesses manufacturing pharmaceutical products.
